key_facts: The role was Class A Driver. On Sept. 22, 2023, Swift driver recruiters Robin Kaufman and Matt Hutto emailed Plaintiff through Tenstreet about completing a Class A Driver application. On Sept. 25, Tenstreet posted a DriverIQ employment document and an FMCSA Clearinghouse result; FMCSA emailed that SWIFT TRANSPORTATION CO OF ARIZONA LLC (USDOT 54283) had requested Clearinghouse access. On Sept. 26, Swift Recruiting emailed an encrypted pre-adverse letter, later decrypted. On Oct. 5, Swift sent a post-adverse letter stating it had decided not to employ Plaintiff based in whole or in part on consumer reports from Asurint, Tenstreet, DriverIQ, FMCSA-DOT, and Equifax Work Number. The decrypted packet is pleaded as known fact: National Criminal without Sex Offender Clear; federal criminal Clear; completed county criminal Clear; NSOPW remained Processing on every snapshot furnished to Plaintiff; the furnished packet contains neither a completed hit nor a completed no-record, and no California source-of-record line; Clearinghouse Driver Not Prohibited. The file does not contain a written offer, a terminal assignment, or a rate of pay. The § 290 count is information and belief that Swift used preliminary sex-offender-registry information from that in-process NSOPW component, in whole or in part, in the denial. What the completed criminal / MVR / PSP / CDLIS components contain is not information disclosed pursuant to Penal Code § 290.46. Do not treat this packet as proof that Home Depot, Best Buy, or AT&T used the registry.
procedural_status: LOCKED. Executed verified complaint and San Joaquin intake dated September 8, 2026; signed, not yet filed. Class A Driver role confirmed. The 290 count is I&B that Swift used preliminary registry information from the still-Processing NSOPW component. Furnished snapshots contain neither a completed hit nor a completed no-record. ICRAA is no longer treated as load-bearing. CCRAA is the alternative if the reports were ordinary consumer reports. § 290 is the fourth count. Serve the current SOS agent (proposed NRAI). File before September 26 if the pre-adverse is accrual. Do not bury Serrato disclosures that day.
damages: No wage rate or hours are in the record. Portfolio valuation is the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $45,000 / $65,000 / $90,000. The 290 damages claim is the healthier statutory path; ICRAA is an alternative notice count rebuilt around § 1786.40(a). Contingent statutory remedies: ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater; CCRAA § 1785.31 if the reports were ordinary consumer reports; UCL restitution of vested money/property only; Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) if preliminary registry use is proven. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers.
risk: The packet shows NSOPW Processing, not a completed hit. The 290 count is I&B that Swift used preliminary registry information from that in-process component. A demurrer can take the printed snapshots as pleaded. It cannot decide, without the adjudication log, whether preliminary NSOPW information was used. If production shows a completed no-record and no preliminary use, 290 dies then. ICRAA/UCL do not need a hit. CCP § 338(a) from Sept. 26, 2023 runs to Sept. 26, 2026. Diversity removal is likely.
